kill_fact:
The catalyst survives every attack. The floor does not survive as stated, because its largest component is a forecast rather than a balance. Start with what is genuinely clean: the event is real, live, unfired and accelerating. The 24 July 2026 results release, filed as Exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K the same day, says in the company's own words 'the planned Ziggo Group spin-off as early as mid-2027', and its forward-looking-statements section names 'the planned spin-off of the Ziggo Group in 2027 and the listing of its shares on Euronext Amsterdam'. There is no record date, no listing prospectus and no scheduled shareholder vote - the 10-Q filed the same day contains no spin-off disclosure at all beyond generic risk language - so SOFT_EXTENDED is the correct label, and the roughly eleven-month distance is real. Nothing has fired, nothing has slipped, and the spread has not closed: the stock closed 27 July 2026 at $9.59, a 52-week low against a $13.12 high. No hidden disqualifier exists either - no going concern, no ATM, no dilution, no financing contingency, no CVR, no second request. The Vodafone transaction has all approvals in hand.

The failure is in the downside. The entry credits $5.86 a share of holding-company cash, drawn from management's raised ~$2.0 billion year-end target, and calls the resulting $8.00 a 'verified floor'. It is not verified. Footnote 4 of the release defines the $2.0 billion as 'our expected cash position at December 31, 2026' - a guided number five months forward. The balance sheet filed the same day says something different: consolidated cash of $2,418.6 million at 30 June 2026, of which Liberty Global on a standalone basis holds $0, unrestricted subsidiaries hold $1,610.1 million, and $808.5 million sits inside the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups where the holding company cannot freely reach it. The 10-Q is explicit that only the $1,610.1 million 'represented available liquidity at the corporate level'. Separately-managed-account investments add just $76.2 million. Against that stands note 4 of the same 10-Q: the purchase of Vodafone's 50% of VodafoneZiggo costs EUR 1.0 billion ($1.1 billion) in cash plus a 10% equity interest in the new Benelux holding company, and 'is expected to close no later than July 31, 2026' - days after the entry date. Pro-forma that payment and corporate cash is roughly $0.5 billion, about $1.50 a share, not $5.86. Getting from there to ~$2.0 billion by 31 December requires roughly $1.4 billion of further inflows in five months from disposals that have not executed: the Wyre stake sale, guided only to year-end 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, and additional Liberty Growth realisations. Roughly 58% of the gross floor build is a plan, not an asset.

Two further quality-of-cash problems compound it. About $340 million of the ~$1.2 billion of year-to-date 'asset monetizations' is a EUR 300 million loan secured against the Wyre stake - borrowed money encumbering the very asset the next checkpoint depends on selling, counted in the raised cash target. And there is no company bid whatsoever: the 10-Q states that no share repurchase program has been approved for 2026 and that the company is not authorized to repurchase any shares during 2026, so the bear's 'no buyback' point is a primary-source fact rather than an inference, and no mechanism exists for one to appear before 2027.

What this does to the trade: on spot values, with the entry's own 50% haircut to the growth portfolio and the operating telecoms at zero, the floor is nearer $4.00 to $4.50 a share. The $8.00 figure only holds if the second-half disposal programme lands as guided, or if the telecoms are credited above zero - which they arguably should be, since Telenet alone earned EUR 347.8 million of Adjusted EBITDA in the quarter and the company will own 100% of VodafoneZiggo after closing. But that is a multiple-of-earnings argument, not the asset-backing argument the entry makes. The asymmetry survives directionally; the advertised -17% downside and the 5.3-to-1 ratio do not.
corrections:
1) MATERIAL - the floor's cash line is a forecast, not a balance. The entry's $5.86 a share comes from a guided 31 December 2026 target (release footnote 4: 'Reflects our expected cash position at December 31, 2026'). Verified spot corporate liquidity is $1,610.1 million at 30 June 2026, per the 10-Q ($0 at Liberty Global standalone, $1,610.1 million at unrestricted subsidiaries, $808.5 million trapped in the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups), plus $76.2 million of SMA investments. EUR 1.0 billion ($1.1 billion) leaves by 31 July 2026 for the Vodafone stake, taking pro-forma corporate cash to roughly $0.5 billion, about $1.50 a share. Reaching ~$2.0 billion needs ~$1.4 billion of unexecuted second-half inflows. Restate the floor: on spot values with the same 50% portfolio haircut and telecoms at zero it is ~$4.00-4.50, not $8.00. Downside from $9.59 is therefore not the stated -17%, and 5.3-to-1 is overstated. If the board wants to keep an ~$8 floor it must be justified on the telecoms being worth something rather than on cash-plus-portfolio backing.
2) MATERIAL - the bear thesis is wrong in the opposite direction and must be struck. Both the bear thesis and the valley-of-death section assert that the ~$2.0 billion 'is the purchase price for Vodafone's half of the Dutch business' and 'converts into an illiquid, leveraged telecom equity'. Per 10-Q note 4 the consideration is EUR 1.0 billion ($1.1 billion) cash plus a 10% equity interest in the new Benelux holdco - not $2.0 billion - and the $2.0 billion is defined as the post-closing year-end position. The correct criticism is not that the cash is committed; it is that the cash is forecast.
3) MINOR - quality of the raised target. The upgrade from ~$1.5 billion is attributed in footnote 4 to (i) the EUR 300 million (~$340 million) asset-backed loan on the Wyre stake and (ii) higher-than-anticipated Liberty Growth disposals. Item (i) is debt, not monetisation, and is secured on the asset whose sale is the next scheduled checkpoint. Net of it, the year-end target is ~$1.66 billion, about $4.87 a share even if fully delivered.
4) MINOR - portfolio mark. Footnote 3 states the $2.9 billion fair market value includes the consolidated investments in Egg, Formula E and Liberty Blume and 'reflects fair value adjustments for certain investments that have a higher estimated fair value than reported book value', and 'Includes listed stakes in ITV and Lionsgate'. So it is a written-up, partly mark-to-market figure rather than a pure private appraisal. Separately, the same release's descriptive section values the Liberty Growth platform (~70 companies and funds) at $3.4 billion, unreconciled with the $2.9 billion FMV cited two pages earlier; the dossier's $8.50-a-share line rests on the smaller of two unexplained numbers. The 50% haircut in the bear case already absorbs this.
5) MINOR, strengthens the bear - the 'no buyback' claim is understated. The 10-Q states plainly that no share repurchase program has been approved by the board for 2026 and that the company is not authorized to repurchase any shares during 2026. This is not a pause in buying; there is no authorization to resume before 2027.
6) NO CORRECTION NEEDED - catalyst status and the Q2 tape. 'As early as mid-2027' verifies verbatim in the filed release, as does the acceleration framing and the conditional 'up to $14 per Liberty share'. Revenue $1,172.0m (-7.7% reported, -6.0% rebased), Adjusted EBITDA $324.9m (-3.1%), Adjusted FCF -$150.4m in the quarter and -$469.7m for the half, net loss $357.8m, VMO2 -7.9% rebased with 28,200 broadband and 63,000 postpaid losses, VodafoneZiggo +7,200 broadband and +31,700 postpaid, EdgeConneX exited for $604m at >30% IRR, portfolio top five >50% of $2.9bn - all confirmed. The half-year cash burn of $469.7m is worse than the dossier's quarterly figure conveys and should be carried forward. The breach of the original $9.50 floor is confirmed: 52-week low $9.30, close $9.59 on 27 July 2026.

This is the primary-source basis for the correction that corporate cash pro-forma the EUR 1.0 billion payment is roughly $0.5 billion (~$1.50/share), not the $5.86/share the floor assumes.

Same 10-Q, Part II Item 5, issuer purchases of equity securities: '(b) No share repurchase program has been approved by our board of directors for 2026, and therefore, at this time, we are not authorized to repurchase any shares during 2026.'
